data.title: Energy Transfer Completes Acquisition of Vaquero Midstream
data.description:
Energy Transfer LP (TXSE: ET) has completed its previously announced acquisition of Vaquero Midstream LLC. Total consideration for the transaction was $1.95 billion in cash and approximately 33.3 million newly issued Energy Transfer common units.

The acquired assets add the Caymus Processing Complex, which includes three processing trains with a total capacity of approximately 675 MMcf/d and approximately 300 miles of pipeline serving leading operators across some of the most active areas of the Delaware Basin.

The transaction is expected to further strengthen Energy Transfer's Permian footprint by increasing access to growing natural gas and NGL production volumes while enhancing connectivity to the Partnership's broader midstream platform.

Energy Transfer LP (TXSE: ET) owns and operates one of the largest and most diversified portfolios of energy assets in the United States, with approximately 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. Energy Transfer’s strategic network spans 44 states with assets in all of the major U.S. production basins. Energy Transfer is a publicly traded limited partnership with core operations that include complementary natural gas midstream, intrastate and interstate transportation and storage assets; crude oil, natural gas liquids (“NGL”) and refined product transportation and terminalling assets; and NGL fractionation. Energy Transfer also owns the general partner interests, the incentive distribution rights and approximately 28 million common units (representing 15% of the aggregate outstanding common units and Class D units) of Sunoco LP (TXSE: SUN), the managing member interests in SunocoCorp LLC (TXSE: SUNC), and the general partner interests and approximately 46 million common units (representing 32% of the outstanding common units) of USA Compression Partners, LP (TXSE: USAC). For more information, visit the Energy Transfer LP website at www.energytransfer.com.

Sunoco LP (TXSE: SUN) is a leading energy infrastructure and fuel distribution master limited partnership operating across 33 countries and territories in North America, the Greater Caribbean, and Europe. SUN's midstream operations include an extensive network of approximately 14,000 miles of pipeline and over 170 terminals. This critical infrastructure complements SUN's fuel distribution operations which distribute over 17 billion gallons annually to approximately 11,000 Sunoco and partner-branded retail locations, as well as independent dealers and commercial customers. SUN's general partner is owned by Energy Transfer LP. For more information, visit the Sunoco LP website at www.sunocolp.com.

SunocoCorp LLC (TXSE: SUNC) is a publicly traded limited liability company that owns a direct limited partner interest in Sunoco LP. For more information, visit the Sunoco LP website at www.sunocolp.com.

USA Compression Partners, LP (TXSE: USAC) is one of the nation’s largest independent providers of natural gas compression services in terms of total compression fleet horsepower. USAC partners with a broad customer base composed of producers, processors, gatherers, and transporters of natural gas and crude oil. USAC focuses on providing midstream natural gas compression services to infrastructure applications primarily in high-volume gathering systems, processing facilities, and transportation applications. For more information, visit the USAC website at www.usacompression.com.

data.title: Australia's NextDC raises annual forecast on sales growth, cost savings
data.description:
Australia's NextDC on Friday raised its fiscal 2027 net revenue and underlying operating earnings forecasts, as the data centre operator gained from strong growth and its cost-cutting measures.

Last week, NextDC paused all projects lacking customer contracts after a major setback at its flagship M3 data centre in Melbourne, where expansion was suspended over power delays and community backlash.

The same setbacks forced the firm to cut its earnings forecast last month, including its capital expenditure plans.

The company expects annual net revenue of A$485 million to A$500 million ($323.11 million - $333.10 million), up from its previous guidance of A$475 million to A$500 million.

It forecast full-year underlying earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) to be between A$260 million and A$275 million, compared with its previous guidance of A$245 million to A$265 million.

The upgraded guidance continues to exclude the revenue and attributable EBITDA of the affected customer contracts at M3, NextDC said.

($1 = 1.5011 Australian dollars)

data.title: P&G to Cut Up to 30% of Product-Supply Workers Amid Automation Push
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Procter & Gamble said it plans to cut 20% to 30% of its product-supply jobs by 2030, as it implements more automation into its supply chain.

The consumer goods company said the job cuts, which will include contractors, are part of its ongoing effort to lower supply-chain costs.

P&G expects to deliver $1.8 billion in annual productivity savings by the end of this decade, in part from the workforce reduction, Chief Product Supply Officer Luc Reynaert said during an investor day event Thursday.

Product supply is also becoming more automated, Reynaert said. "Success heavily depends on a workforce with the skills to scale and optimize these technologies," he said.

P&G has been working for several years to improve its supply chain through a program it calls Supply 3.0. The plan involves keeping supply steady, digitizing and automating the supply chain, training its workforce on those new tools, and improving sustainability.

Eventually, P&G is aiming for 90% or greater free cash flow productivity from the improvements.

"Supply 3.0 is not a destination. It is the foundation that will evolve us into the supply chain of the future," Reynaert said.

P&G didn't immediately respond to a request for comment about the job cuts.

data.title: Anthropic's stock surges in its debut - and the rest of the market dives anyway
data.description:
By Joy Wiltermuth and Joseph Adinolfi

All four major U.S. stock indexes are now on pace for their worst week since President Trump's 'liberation day' tariffs of April 2025

The stock market is convulsing despite a hugely successful IPO from Anthropic on Thursday.

Neither a wildly successful first-ever IPO from an artificial-intelligence lab, nor a blockbuster earnings report from arguably the most important company in the AI trade, were enough to stop the carnage in the U.S. stock market this week.

Earlier this week, Nvidia (NVDA) passed a big "earnings test" after the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang - but its stock fell anyway. Then, on Thursday, Anthropic's (ANT) hugely anticipated IPO passed the market's next big "valuation test," with the AI lab's stock opening 34% above its $83 IPO price, before it closed at $97.17.

Yet the S&P 500 index SPX still tumbled 2% Thursday to close at 7,175.83, as a broad-based selloff left each of the index's 11 sectors in the red for a second time in three days, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

"I'm a bit surprised that we are cascading here," said Mark Arbeter, president of Arbeter Investments. He expected Nivida's earnings and Anthropic's successful IPO to calm the market, allow it to bottom "at least on a short-term basis" and open the door to "a decent snapback rally."

Instead, the S&P 500 stayed below its 200-day moving average, a crucial support level, and was edging closer to the 7,000 mark. Any close below 7,037.04 would officially land the S&P 500 in a correction, or a drop of at least 10% from its previous peak, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

To be sure, corrections of 10% are considered normal, and the stock market isn't the U.S. economy, which lately has been showing signs of speeding up.

"Technically, it's been a long time since we've had a significant downturn in the market, and I think we are due," said David Kelly, chief global strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management. "I don't think it's much more than that."

Kelly doesn't think "the amount of money raised by Anthropic sucked the market dry." Instead, if there's any problem, it's that people's portfolios have become overly concentrated, he said. Furthermore, he thinks nothing about the economy's resilience has changed. "People should try to stay calm," he added.

Still, while past dips in stocks were bought, now there appears to be "a lot of losing hands holding equities right now," said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist at LPL Financial.

Lately, when stocks have opened higher, the market has failed to hold those gains through the close. Turnquist noted. "Sentiment has clearly changed in the market," he said.

To put a finer point on the scope of Thursday's selloff, only 38 stocks in the S&P 500 rose on Thursday - the fewest since Dec. 31, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The heavy losses had the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA down 6.2% for the week and teetering on the edge of correction territory.

The S&P 500 was off 5.1% for the week, while the Nasdaq Composite COMP was 5% lower and the Russell 2000 index RUT of small-cap stocks was off 4.9%. If those declines hold, it would be the worst week for all four indexes since the "liberation day" tariff selloff in the week of April 4, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

-Joy Wiltermuth -Joseph Adinolfi

data.title: Partner teams from collapsing law firm Weil join Sullivan & Cromwell, Milbank, Simpson Thacher
data.description:
By Sara Merken

Teams of lawyers from Weil, Gotshal & Manges are joining Sullivan & Cromwel, Milbank and Simpson Thacher, adding to the growing diaspora of Weil lawyers amid the 95-year-old law firm's dissolution.

Sullivan & Cromwell on Thursday said at least 12 lawyers will join in New York from Weil's highly regarded restructuring practice, including Gary Holtzer, a former leader of the group, and current US restructuring co-chair Ronit Berkovich.

Weil partners Kelly DiBlasi and Jessica Liou, as well as counsel Alejandro Bascoy, will also join Sullivan & Cromwell as partners in its restructuring and special situations group, the firm said.

Meanwhile, Milbank said on Thursday that it will launch in Paris with Weil's entire team there, comprising 22 partners and 87 lawyers in total. The group includes David Aknin, who will be global co-head of Milbank's private equity practice, and Yannick Piette, who will serve as global co-head of its public M&A practice.

Later in the day, Simpson Thacher said it added more lawyers from Weil in California and New York, adding to earlier recent hires from the firm. The group includes Kyle Krpata, co-chair of Weil's corporate department and its US private equity practice; Tana Ryan, managing partner of Weil's Los Angeles office; and Craig Adas, co-managing partner of its Silicon Valley Office, alongside other private equity and M&A lawyers.

Law firms have been heavily recruiting Weil lawyers since the firm first said in late October that it planned to wind down following a string of key partner departures in recent months. The moves announced this week extended into Weil's core restructuring practice, which had been a major revenue driver for the firm.

Skadden said on Wednesday it was adding a team of about 40 restructuring and corporate lawyers from Weil, including 11 partners. Matt Barr, who led Weil's restructuring practice, will become the head of Skadden's global restructuring group, the firm said.

Several other law firms, including Kirkland & Ellis and Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher, have picked up large teams from Weil. Sidley Austin on Wednesday said it hired 14 partners as part of a 35-lawyer group in New York, across multiple practice areas. Cleary Gottlieb and Latham & Watkins are among the growing list of other firms that have brought on Weil attorneys so far.

Sullivan & Cromwell co-chairs Robert Giuffra and Scott Miller in a statement said the Weil team joining the firm "has advised on many of the largest and most complex chapter 11 cases, cross-border restructurings and liability management transactions of the past two decades."

data.title: Onar Holding Reports $13.5M Pro Forma Nine-Month Revenue After Acquisition
data.description:
Onar Holding reported nine-month revenue of $3.13 million and a net loss of $3.61 million for the period ended September 30, 2026, which included two days of results from its acquisition of Advertise Purple. On a pro forma basis, combining both businesses for the full nine months, revenue was $13.52 million and net loss was $1.25 million. The company said it used $0.59 million of cash in operating activities during the nine months.

Financial Highlights

  • Third-quarter revenue was $1.06 million; nine-month revenue was $3.13 million.
  • Unaudited pro forma revenue, assuming Advertise Purple had been owned since January 1, was $4.44 million for the third quarter and $13.52 million for the nine months.
  • Net loss was $1.36 million for the third quarter and $3.61 million for the nine months. Pro forma net loss was $0.61 million and $1.25 million, respectively.
  • Cash used in operating activities was $0.59 million for the nine months. Total liabilities were $37.7 million at September 30, compared with $9.7 million at the start of the year.
  • The company reported a working capital deficit of approximately $15.2 million and said its filings continue to describe substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern.

Business Highlights

  • Onar acquired Advertise Purple on September 29, a performance-based affiliate and partnership marketing business, along with its Bloom affiliate performance data platform.
  • The combined companies serve approximately 400 clients. Advertise Purple continues to be led by its core team, five members of which signed employment agreements with Onar.
  • Onar said its JUICE business is running Advertise Purple’s marketing and referring new business, while Advertise Purple’s sales team is sending leads to JUICE.
  • Cortex, Onar’s attribution platform, began billing subscription clients in July and completed its first full quarter of recurring billings.
  • Onar is pursuing a Nasdaq Capital Market listing and is in the application and preparation stage. A 1-for-250 reverse stock split was approved but had not taken effect as of the letter.

data.title: Intuit Q1 Profit Rises, Raises FY27 Revenue Outlook; To Sell Mailchimp
data.description:
MOUNTAIN VIEW (dpa-AFX) - Intuit Inc. (INTU), the financial technology company behind TurboTax, QuickBooks and Credit Karma, reported an increase in profit for the first quarter, with results exceeding the top end of its guidance.

The company also raised its full-year revenue outlook and announced a deal to sell its email marketing platform Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for approximately $3.68 billion.

Net income for the quarter increased to $695 million or $2.59 per share from $446 million or $1.59 per share in the year-ago period. On an adjusted basis, net income rose to $780 million or $2.91 per share.

Total revenue for the quarter grew 12% to $4.35 billion from $3.89 billion a year earlier.

Global Business Solutions revenue advanced 15% to $3.1 billion, with Online Ecosystem revenue rising 20% to $2.4 billion. Consumer revenue increased 7% to $958 million.

Under the agreement, Bending Spoons will acquire Mailchimp for about $3.68 billion, consisting of $3.31 billion in cash and $368 million in Bending Spoons stock. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. Intuit intends to use the cash proceeds to repurchase shares during fiscal 2027 following the closing.

For fiscal 2027, Intuit now expects revenue of $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion, compared with its previous forecast of $23.279 billion to $23.512 billion. The company reiterated its full-year earnings per share outlook of $20.12 to $20.36 and adjusted earnings per share forecast of $22.88 to $23.12.

For the second quarter, Intuit expects revenue of $4.931 billion to $4.954 billion, earnings per share of $2.55 to $2.60 and adjusted earnings per share of $3.17 to $3.22. The guidance does not include any impact from the pending Mailchimp sale.

data.title: Ellington Credit Company Announces Financial Results for the Second Fiscal Quarter Ended September 30, 2026
data.description:
Ellington Credit Company () ("we") today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

  • Net asset value (NAV) per share was $4.04 as of September 30, 2026, which includes the effects of distributions of $0.24 per share for the quarter.

  • GAAP net income was $3.7 million, or $0.09 per share.

  • Net investment income ("NII") was $6.7 million, or $0.17 per share.
    • Adjusted net investment income1 was $6.7 million, or $0.17 per share.



  • CLO portfolio was $332.0 million as of September 30, 2026.
    • CLO debt investments—$146.4 million

    • CLO equity investments—$185.6 million

    • Purchased $41.5 million of CLO investments and sold $31.5 million, across 61 trades.



  • Weighted average GAAP yield2 for the quarter, based on amortized cost, was 12.9% on the total CLO portfolio.

  • Received $14.5 million in recurring cash distributions3 from the CLO portfolio, or $0.37 per share.

  • Raised net proceeds of $5.5 million through the issuance of approximately 1.27 million common shares at prices representing a 3% weighted average premium to NAV per share.

  • Subsequent to quarter end, reset our monthly distribution rate to $0.05 per share, effective with the distribution payable in January 2027.

Management Commentary

“Ellington Credit generated an economic return of 2.4% for the third calendar quarter, or 9.9% annualized, as our active trading and disciplined risk management helped us navigate renewed market volatility,” said Laurence Penn, Chief Executive Officer and President. “Our CLO mezzanine debt and equity portfolios both contributed positively, led by net investment income. Our credit hedges generated gains for the quarter and helped protect NAV per share as credit spreads widened in September. These positive contributions were partially offset by losses on interest rate hedges associated with our fixed-rate unsecured notes. We are proud to have continued our relative outperformance, generating positive GAAP earnings in a challenging quarter when the vast majority of our peers reported losses.

“We remained highly active during the quarter, executing 61 distinct CLO trades and continuing to rotate capital toward investments where we see more attractive risk-adjusted returns. Our overall portfolio size was roughly unchanged quarter over quarter, as sales, paydowns and deal calls largely offset new investment activity. Importantly, the weighted average yield on assets acquired during the quarter increased to 16.7%, up from 14.9% in the second quarter.

“Adjusted net investment income increased by $0.02 sequentially to $0.17 per share, and we continue to see opportunities for further increases through additional capital deployment, selective use of leverage, and continued portfolio rotation. Our Board of Trustees has reset our monthly distribution rate to $0.05 per share, or $0.15 per quarter, a level supported by our current NII. We believe that this positions us to maintain an attractive, sustainable distribution that is well covered by net investment income, while also building NAV per share.”

CLO Performance

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Morningstar LSTA U.S. Leveraged Loan Index generated a total return of 1.9%, despite persistent credit dispersion and renewed volatility toward quarter end. Returns were supported by investor demand for floating-rate assets, a recovery in certain discounted loans, particularly in the software sector, and refinancings and maturity extensions. Double-B- and single-B-rated loans generated positive returns over the quarter, while triple-C-rated loans underperformed as rising interest rates pressured highly leveraged borrowers, particularly in cable and telecommunications. Loan prices declined in late September amid heightened inflation concerns and broader market volatility.

The European leveraged loan market underperformed the U.S. market, with more pronounced weakness in lower-quality credits. Headwinds included uncertainty over France’s fiscal and political outlook, energy-price volatility, and some forced selling from European credit funds.

CLO performance was mixed, as constructive loan-market technicals were tempered by the late-quarter selloff. Within CLO mezzanine debt, shorter-spread-duration, more seasoned positions benefited from stronger performance in shorter-maturity loans and principal paydowns that reduced deal-level leverage and strengthened structural credit protections. Meanwhile, higher-quality CLO equity positions with longer reinvestment periods benefited from stronger-than-anticipated interest payments in July, while limited loan repricing activity continued to support excess spread and equity cash flows.

However, higher borrowing costs pressured highly leveraged borrowers, weighing on CLO investments — particularly European CLO equity and lower-rated debt positions — with greater exposure to lower-quality collateral. In September, CLO tranche spreads widened modestly, and CLO equity valuations came under renewed pressure as broader markets weakened.

Our CLO mezzanine debt and equity portfolios each generated positive results for the quarter, as net investment income more than offset net realized and unrealized losses in our CLO equity investments. Credit hedges generated gains for the quarter overall, including in September, helping cushion the impact of that month’s spread widening on NAV per share. Additional headwinds included losses on interest rate hedges associated with our unsecured notes, and mark-to-market losses on the notes themselves as credit spread tightening more than offset the impact of higher interest rates.

We executed 61 distinct CLO trades during the quarter, with sales and paydowns largely offsetting new investment activity. The weighted average yield on assets acquired during the quarter increased to 16.7%, compared with 14.9% in the second quarter. At September 30, 2026, our CLO portfolio had a fair value of $332.0 million and a weighted average projected yield of 18.3% based on fair value.

Reconciliation of Adjusted Net Investment Income to Net Investment Income

We calculate Adjusted Net Investment Income as net investment income adjusted for: (i) non-recurring expenses; (ii) non-capitalized transaction costs, (iii) net realized and change in net appreciation (depreciation) associated with periodic settlements on interest rate swaps, and (iv) interest and dividend income (expense) net of transaction fees associated with the referenced assets on total return swaps. Adjusted Net Investment Income is a supplemental non-GAAP financial measure. We believe that the presentation of Adjusted Net Investment Income provides information useful to investors, because: (i) we believe that it is a useful indicator of both current and projected long-term financial performance, in that it excludes the impact of certain expenses and non-capitalized transaction costs that we believe are less useful in forecasting long-term performance and distribution-paying ability; and (ii) we believe that realized and accrued periodic settlements on interest rates swaps and interest and dividend income (expense) net of transaction fees on total return swaps are similar to net investment income and are more appropriately classified as recurring.

Our calculation of Adjusted Net Investment Income may differ from the calculation of similarly titled non-GAAP financial measures by our peers, with the result that these non-GAAP financial measures might not be directly comparable. In addition, because Adjusted Net Investment Income is an incomplete measure of our financial results and differs from net investment income computed in accordance with U.S. GAAP, it should be considered supplementary to, and not as a substitute for, net investment income computed in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

In setting our distributions, our Board of Trustees considers our earnings, liquidity, financial condition, distribution requirements, and financial covenants, along with other factors that our Board of Trustees may deem relevant from time to time.

data.title: GOP Effort to Pass $350 Billion In Extra Military Spending Stalls In Lame Duck — WSJ
data.description:
By Lindsay Wise, Marcus Weisgerber and Yoko Kubota

WASHINGTON — Senate Republicans are suspending their effort to pass $350 billion in additional military spending, as momentum fades to pay for the Iran war and other defense priorities before the GOP loses control of Congress in January.

The stalled push — which would have required near unanimity among Republicans and a cumbersome process — comes just weeks after Democrats captured large majorities in the House and Senate amid widespread backlash to the war and high prices in midterm elections.

The Pentagon in April requested a $350 billion spending package that included billions of dollars for Trump administration priorities, including a missile shield, ships, aircraft and satellites. It also included billions for replacing depleted munitions stocks. The package was in addition to a $1.1 trillion annual base budget requested by the Pentagon.

Republicans, who currently hold 53 Senate seats, would need to use a process known as budget reconciliation that lets them advance some bills with a simple majority. That enables them to sidestep Democrats and the Senate's usual 60-vote threshold.

But GOP senators would have had to remain almost completely united through a marathon amendment process that would allow Democrats to force dozens of politically painful votes. And the fate of the effort in the House was uncertain because of the cost and the difficulty of corralling the necessary votes, given the chamber's slim majority and postelection attendance problems.

"We've got a lot of work to do because we have competing priorities, and I don't think we have the votes yet," said Sen. Thom Tillis (R., N.C.), who said he would have backed the reconciliation package if he thought it would survive the House.

Some conservative Republicans in the House and Senate have raised objections to the lack of provisions that would cover some of the costs of the package, including Rep. Mike Rogers (R., Ala.), chair of the House Armed Services Committee, who warned Tuesday at the Hudson Institute that a $350 billion reconciliation package is "not going to happen." He said it would have to slim down to about $100 billion.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said last week that the Pentagon needed "$350 billion at a minimum for reconciliation" in order "to make a generational and historic investment" in the military.

"Right now, we're flooding the zone because this lame duck period is critically important for funding of our department," Hegseth said.

Sen. Rand Paul (R., Ky.) bashed the $350 billion proposal as tone deaf and irresponsible, especially in the immediate aftermath of the midterms. More than six in 10 voters said the U.S. made the wrong decision in taking military action against Iran, according to results from a poll of more than 79,000 registered voters, conducted for the Associated Press and all the major television and cable-news networks.

"The last thing Republicans want to be remembered by, being in leadership, is spending money, adding to the debt and financing the Iran war?" said Paul, who has been a vocal opponent of the conflict. "I mean, it's completely tone deaf, a huge mistake, and I'm not voting for a pure Republican reconciliation bill that just adds to the debt."

But some vulnerable Republicans had said they were willing to support the partisan package. Sen. Ted Budd (R., N.C.) is up for re-election in 2028 in North Carolina, where Democrats swept to victory across the state earlier this month, flipping a Senate seat and at least six U.S. House seats. Budd said he is thinking of troops at Fort Bragg and Camp Lejeune. "We've got so much defense in our state," said Budd. "I want to make sure we take care of them."

Still, Budd said he wants the war to come to an end soon. "I want it in the rearview mirror," he said. "But in order to do so we have to give our men and women in uniform the tools they need, the ammunition they need to make sure they are successful."

Despite the political risks, Budd and other Republicans said they were motivated to secure the additional defense funding partly because they think Democrats will refuse to help them pass it on a bipartisan basis. And they don't want spending on the Iran war to become a bargaining chip in talks to avert a government shutdown next month.

But after hours of private talks on Tuesday, Senate Republicans said they would try to pass military spending with Democrats before heading down the one-party path.

Sen. Mitch McConnell (R., Ky.), who chairs the subcommittee responsible for funding the Pentagon, said reconciliation should never have been a substitute for finishing work on the annual military spending bill.

"The way to show we're serious about defense is to build new investments into sustainable, full-year appropriations," he said in a statement to The Wall Street Journal, adding "let's get it done."

The clock is ticking. Funding for the federal government will lapse after Dec. 11 unless Congress acts. At a closed-door lunch on Tuesday, Senate Democrats discussed blocking war spending as a condition of funding the government, but they made no decisions, said Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D., Md.).

Van Hollen, who recently launched a long shot bid to unseat the Senate's longtime Democratic leader, Chuck Schumer (D., N.Y.), has called for shutting down the government over the war.

But on Tuesday he suggested Democrats could accept an amendment vote, at a minimum. "My view is that we, at the very least, need to have an amendment that clearly provides an opportunity for people to vote to not fund the offensive operations in this illegal war," he said.

Schumer hasn't threatened a shutdown, but he promised the day after the election that Democrats would end the war, using Congress's "power of the purse" if necessary.

"We don't want to shut down the government," Schumer told reporters Wednesday. "It's up to Republicans to roll up their sleeves and work with us to avoid that from happening. We don't know where they're at right now."

Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg, a private equity billionaire, made a last-ditch pitch for the $350 billion at a closed-door Senate Republican lunch on Wednesday, staying for an hour-and-a-half to answer Republicans' questions. He also invited Democrats to a classified briefing in a secure room elsewhere in the Capitol.

The Pentagon is working with lawmakers to map out which high-priority programs that span several years — such as munitions, aircraft and Trump's Golden Dome — can be moved into the military's base budget, a senior defense official said. The official said the Pentagon officials have met at this point with every member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, Republican and Democrat.

The offer to brief Democrats came after Sen. Mike Rounds, (R., S.D.) on Tuesday at a Navy confirmation hearing said Democrats have been excluded from top secret threat briefings the Pentagon has given to Republican lawmakers.

"Pretty tough to ask all of my colleagues to support that if they're not even invited in to hear the information in the first place," he said, noting appropriations need bipartisan support to pass in the Senate.

data.title: AMD Sheds $67 Billion as Anthropic Debuts — WSJ
data.description:
By Vicky Ge Huang

Shares of AMD fell sharply Thursday as individual investors sold the chipmaker to fund their Anthropic purchases and an investment firm issued a report questioning the company's China exposure.

AMD dropped 7.7%, erasing roughly $67 billion in market value. The stock was the second-worst performer in the Nasdaq 100 index.

Individual investors have been unloading AMD and other AI stocks to free up cash for Anthropic's debut, according to retail flow-tracking firm Vanda Research. Thirteen out of 17 AI names tracked by Vanda saw net selling, with AMD leading the outflows.

AMD shares were also weighed down after Hunterbrook disclosed a short position and issued a report alleging that "AMD firmware keeps turning up at a blacklisted Chinese company." An AMD spokesman said the claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships.

data.title: Celldex declines as it abandons barzolvolimab in atopic dermatitis
data.description:
Key points:
  • Celldex is down ~2% in after-hours trading Thursday after reporting that a phase 2 trial of barzolvolimab for atopic dermatitis missed its primary and secondary goals.
  • The percent change in weekly average in Peak Pruritus Numerical Rating Scale (PP-NRS) score at week 16 compared to placebo did not have a statistically significant difference. Also, secondary endpoints, change in baseline Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score, and the percentage of patients with Investigator's Global Assessment ("IGA") score of 0 or 1, were not met.
  • Barzolvolimab remains in a phase 3 study for chronic spontaneous urticaria with Celldex planning to submit a BLA for that indication

data.title: Australia's Mineral Resources names Michael Ellis as CFO from 2027
data.description:
Mineral Resources said on Friday it had appointed Michael Ellis as the company's chief financial officer, effective May 19, 2027.

Ellis will join the Australian miner from mining services provider Perenti , where he has served as finance chief since September 2024.

Ellis has more than 20 years of experience in finance, including over a decade in the mining services sector, MinRes said in a filing to the exchange.

Jonathan Cowper, executive general manager of finance, will serve as acting CFO as previously announced until Ellis takes over, the company added.

The appointment follows MinRes' announcement earlier this month that Mark Wilson, CFO since 2018, will retire at the end of this year.

Wilson remained with the firm through a major governance overhaul as it sought to rebuild its reputation following scandals in late 2024 involving founder Chris Ellison and a series of board departures.

Perenti, in a separate statement, said Ellis would be succeeded by Simon Franich, currently vice president of finance at the company's contract mining division.
